sources.title: Memory chip makers outearn Alphabet, other tech giants on AI demand
Why Intel’s stock saw its worst day in decades — and a $140 billion wipeout

en.title: Memory chip makers outpace Alphabet on AI demand; Intel stock drops
en.dek: Memory chip makers earned more than Alphabet last quarter, while Intel shares fell sharply.
facts: Five leading global memory chip suppliers logged higher total operating and net profits than five major U.S. tech companies last quarter, according to Nikkei Asia.
Investment in data centers has increased memory chip demand, driving profits for memory makers, Nikkei Asia reported.
Intel’s PC business faces pressure as memory-chip prices reduce demand, MarketWatch noted.
Intel shares fell on their worst day in decades, wiping out $140 billion in market value, MarketWatch reported.
body: According to Nikkei Asia, five leading global memory chip suppliers logged higher total operating and net profits than five major U.S. tech companies last quarter. This marks the first time the memory sector has outperformed the tech giants. The surge is linked to increased investment in data centers for artificial intelligence. Memory makers such as Kioxia and Samsung benefited from the spending wave.

Nikkei Asia noted that AI workloads have outpaced supply for now. The demand growth has pushed memory chip prices higher. Higher prices have boosted operating margins for the memory makers. Investors, however, are beginning to question the sustainability of this trend.

MarketWatch reported that Intel’s stock fell sharply on October 30. The decline was the worst in decades for the company. The drop wiped out $140 billion in market value. Intel’s PC business is under pressure as memory-chip prices dent demand and corporate IT teams cut laptop budgets.

The events illustrate how AI demand reshapes the semiconductor market. Memory chip makers gain when AI workloads increase, while PC makers feel the impact of higher memory costs. The market reaction reflects the shifting balance between supply and demand in the tech sector.
en.context: Artificial intelligence requires large amounts of data processing, which relies on memory chips. Companies building AI infrastructure invest heavily in data centers, increasing demand for memory chips. This demand has pushed memory makers' profits higher while raising costs for PC manufacturers.
